ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, $AB$ is the diameter of $\odot O$, and point $P$ is on $\odot O$ with $PA=PB$. Point $M$ is outside $\odot O$, and $MB$ is tangent to $\odot O$ at point $B$. Connect $OM$, and draw $AC\parallel OM$ through point $A$ to intersect with $\odot O$ at point $C$, and connect $BC$ to intersect $OM$ at point $D$. $MC$ is a tangent to $\odot O$. Given that $AB=20$ and $BC=16$, connect $PC$. What is the length of $PC$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Since $AB$ is the diameter of $\odot O$,\\
it follows that $\angle ACB=\angle APB=90^\circ$,\\
Since $AB=20$,\\
we have $PA=PB=\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\times 20=10\sqrt{2}$,\\
Since $BC=16$,\\
we get $AC=\sqrt{AB^{2}-BC^{2}}=\sqrt{20^{2}-16^{2}}=12$,\\
Draw $AH\perp PC$ at point H through point A,\\
thus $\angle AHC=\angle AHP=90^\circ$,\\
Since $\angle ACH=\angle ABP=45^\circ$,\\
we have $AH=CH=AC\times \sin 45^\circ=12\times \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}=6\sqrt{2}$,\\
Therefore, $PH=\sqrt{PA^{2}-AH^{2}}=\sqrt{(10\sqrt{2})^{2}-(6\sqrt{2})^{2}}=8\sqrt{2}$,\\
Hence, $PC=PH+CH=\boxed{14\sqrt{2}}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there is a circle, AB is a horizontal diameter, O is on AB and is the center of the circle; P is above the circle, C is at the lower left of the circle, and A, P, B, C are all on the circle; at the lower right there is an exterior point M of the circle, MB is tangent to the circle at B, and MC is tangent to the circle at C; OM intersects BC at D, and PC is also connected in the figure. Reasoning: Because A, P, B, C are on the same circle, and AB is a diameter, therefore by the inscribed angle subtended by a diameter being a right angle, ∠APB=90°, ∠ACB=90°. Also PA=PB, AB=20, so the right triangle APB is an isosceles right triangle, PA=PB=20/√2=10√2. It is known that BC=16; in the right triangle ABC, AB=20 is the hypotenuse, so AC=√(20^2-16^2)=√144=12. Regard APBC as a cyclic quadrilateral, in the order A-P-B-C; its two diagonals are AB and PC. By Ptolemy's theorem, AB·PC=AP·BC+PB·AC. Substitute the values: 20·PC=(10√2)·16+(10√2)·12=280√2, therefore PC=14√2.
